codeReview.summary: The commit delivers the bulk CSS palette cleanup: `rgba()` backgrounds, `mindfuck-*` classes, `backdrop-filter`/`blur`, and scanline/noise selectors are removed from the frontend CSS surface. However, the implementation stops at deleting the CSS for the galaxy/vignette backdrop effects; the React runtime still renders those decorative layers and still exposes a live vignette control, so the feature does not fully remove the effect path it claims to eliminate.

issues.description: The feature description explicitly called for removing the galaxy parallax star layers and vignette overlay, but this component still renders all three `simulation-galaxy-layer` elements plus `simulation-core-vignette`, and `App.tsx:188-197` still computes parallax transforms for them. The commit only deleted the matching CSS selectors from `index.css`, so the decorative layer implementation is still present as dead DOM/runtime work instead of being fully removed.

The overhauled UI still shows an `edge vignette` slider even though the commit removed the `.simulation-core-vignette` styling from `index.css`. The setting is still clamped in `hooks/useSimulationTuning.ts:142-151` and defaulted in `app/coreSimulationConfig.ts:101-119`, so users are left with a visible control whose target effect was removed. That is a user-facing regression in the exact area this feature was supposed to clean up.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `refactor-worker` says frontend refactors must run lint, but this feature's handoff still marked `followedProcedure: true` after skipping lint entirely. That process gap matters here because the very next frontend feature in repo history is an ESLint-regression cleanup.

summary: Review failed: the CSS cleanup is substantial, but galaxy/vignette effect code and a now-broken vignette control remain wired into the React app, so the feature did not fully remove the decorative backdrop path it claimed to overhaul.
